# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 841
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/841
- **Title**: gh-840 [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-840` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +879
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T13:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T13:53:19Z

## PR Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause
- Live PR #826 (gh-825): `agent:rework` was consumed by the `rework-on-label` rule's `consumeLabels` path (dispatch accepted, or gh-715 cross-anchor suppression while a review leg held the other anchor) — yet no rework leg ever ran, no push, 4/6 threads open, no close marker.
- Consumption is fail-open: nothing records it, and every re-arm path (`arm_rework`) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch, gh-807 verdict gate) — the PR hangs forever.

### Fix
- `js/common/reworkConsumption.js` (new): consumption-audit markers (path + head, machine-author-gated) and the pure `shouldRestoreArm` sweep decision.
- `js/smAgent.js`: both `consumeLabels` branches stamp a gh-840 audit comment on every `agent:rework` consumption; new `restore_rework_arm` localAction re-arms when a consumption is proven bogus (marker evidence, head not advanced, no rework in flight, quiet > `staleMinutes`).
- `sm_github.json`: new `rework-arm-restore` rule (machine PRs, unresolved threads, no label; `staleMinutes: 30` ≈ 6 ticks).

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `js/unit-tests/test_reworkConsumption.js` — 16 tests (marker protocol, AC1 restore, AC2 close proofs, AC3 human-only untouched, grace bound). Registered in `run_all.json`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 9 integration tests replaying the #826 timeline (restore, grace, head-advanced, gh-807 gate preserved, human threads, in-flight leg, audit-on-consume, deployed-rule shape).
- Full suite: **2442 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- gh-807 verdict semantics untouched (non-goal); gh-744 preserved — the sweep counts only machine-authored unresolved threads and requires consumption evidence.
- AC4 (live metric) needs post-ship observation; the sweep self-heals the next occurrence ≤6 ticks by construction.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #841._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# 🚨 BLOCKING: the head is read from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules — the entire gh-840 mechanism is inert in production

Both new code paths derive the head only from the query item:

```javascript
var head = ((ticket.pr && ticket.pr.headSha) || ticket.headSha) || null;   // auditReworkConsumption
var head = reworkLatchHeadOf(ticket);                                       // restoreReworkArm
```

For PR-carrier rules, `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` builds items with **`pr: null`** and only populates `item.pr` when `needsStatus` is true — i.e. when the rule query carries `checks` / `mergeState` / `notMergeState` / `mergeable` / `prChecks` / `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` (see the `needsStatus` block and the gh-807 comment above it). Neither consuming rule qualifies:

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`
- `rework-arm-restore` (this PR): `{"type":"pr","notLabels":["agent:rework"],"threadsResolved":false,"prMachineAuthor":true}` → `item.pr` stays `null` (`threadsResolved` reads threads via a separate provider probe; `prMachineAuthor` reads the free `item.author`)

Live consequences, all silent:

1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. The ticket's "Audit log: every consumption records its path" capability never happens, and the sweep has no evidence to ever act on.
2. **The sweep's head-dependent gates are all dead.** `head === null` → `consultReworkLatch` short-circuits to not-latched (gh-806 latch bypassed), the `hasActiveLegRun` check is skipped entirely (in-flight legs don't block the restore), `headAdvanced` is always `false` (the AC2 "head advanced = close proof" branch never fires), the restore marker records head `'unknown'`, and `armReworkLatch(ticket)` no-ops — so after a restore there is no latch protecting against a stacked dispatch.

The 25 tests pass because every fixture injects `pr: { …, headSha: HEAD }` — a shape the live query layer never produces for these two rules. This is exactly the class of bug the tests were meant to exclude.

**Fix:** probe the head through the existing `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` helper (the same fresh-probe pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses at js/smAgent.js:4065) as a fallback in both `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm`, and log a warning when an `agent:rework` consumption cannot be attributed (fail loud, not `return;`). Add at least one test per path with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`) asserting the probe fallback — that test would have caught this.

Related pre-existing note (not this PR's scope, but it shares the same broken assumption): `arm_rework` (`rework-unresolved-threads`, query has no status keys either) also runs with `item.pr === null`, so its gh-806 latch consult/arm is equally inert on the PR-carrier path — worth a follow-up ticket, since it is one of the three "withheld re-arm" causes named in the gh-840 forensics.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: any head move is treated as a rework close — a silent branch refresh after a bogus consumption defeats the sweep permanently

```javascript
var headAdvanced = !!(newestConsume && newestConsume.head && head &&
    String(newestConsume.head) !== String(head));
...
headAdvancedPastConsumption: headAdvanced,
```

The ticket's AC2 close proof is "comment + head advanced **OR** explicit no-threads-to-own proof". This approximation treats *any* head move as the close marker — but `update_branch` (the silent git-merge refresh, js/smAgent.js `silentUpdateBranch`) pushes a merge commit to the PR head **without resolving review threads and without any rework leg running**. Timeline that breaks the sweep:

1. bogus consumption of `agent:rework` (head `H1`, machine threads unresolved) → consume marker stamped for `H1`;
2. the next refresh tick merges `main` → head advances to `H2`, threads untouched;
3. every subsequent sweep: `unresolvedMachineThreads > 0` but `headAdvanced === true` → `'head-advanced'` → **no restore, forever** — the exact consumed-without-work hang this PR exists to fix, now invisible to the recovery path.

The mitigating re-review loop (stale verdict → re-review → fresh verdict → `arm_rework`) may eventually recover such PRs, but gh-840's own forensics show review legs ran repeatedly on #826 for 4h+ without any re-arm landing — relying on that loop is what made the sweep necessary.

**Suggestion:** only accept `head-advanced` as close proof when corroborated — e.g. require a concluded `ai-teammate.yml` leg run on the current head with `created_at` at/after the consumption timestamp (`headWorkflowRunsSafe` is already fetched two lines above for the in-flight check, so this is cheap), or fall through to restore when unresolved *machine* threads still exist on the advanced head (an advanced head with the same open machine threads is evidence of a refresh, not a close). If the deliberate tradeoff is kept, it should be documented in the rule description in `sm_github.json` so the next incident review doesn't misread `'head-advanced'` skips as healthy closes.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# 💡 SUGGESTION: normalize `pullRequestId` to a string for parity with the sibling readers

```javascript
var raw = github_get_pr_comments({
    workspace: repoInfo.owner, repository: repoInfo.repo,
    pullRequestId: prNumber
});
```

Every other caller of `github_get_pr_comments` / `github_get_pr_review_threads` in this codebase passes `pullRequestId: String(prNumber)` (`readVerdictRecords`, `smProvider.verdictRecords`, `prHeadAndLabels`, …). The bridge most likely tolerates a number, but the PR-carrier `ticket.prNumber` type is not guaranteed across all provider paths, and a coercion difference here would silently return zero markers — which for this sweep is the fail-closed "no evidence" shape and thus hard to notice. `String(prNumber)` for consistency.

---

### Thread 4

# gh-840: [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)

## Description

## Goal

`agent:rework` consumption must be FAIL-CLOSED: the label may be removed ONLY by the rework leg's successful close (threads resolved/pushed + 'rework cycle closed' bookkeeping). A consumption without a rework run, a push, or the closing comment is a bug — today it silently hangs the PR forever.

## Subject

The rework-arm consumption path(s) in the SM tick / rework bookkeeping (gh-822 family). Live instance: dmtools-agents PR #826 (gh-825), 2026-10-10 ~10:00Z: `agent:rework` armed (twice, comments present) and later CONSUMED — yet: no fix commit on the head for the review's blocking defect (normTokenRow drops `cacheRead`), 4/6 review threads still unresolved, no 'rework cycle closed' comment, no rework-leg run on the branch (only review legs since 08:55Z). Result: 4h+ hang — gh-744 correctly refuses auto-resolution, nothing re-arms (correct), but the consumed-without-work arm never returns.

## Capability surface

- Guard: label removal only from the leg-close path (verify a closing marker exists: comment + head advanced OR explicit no-threads-to-own proof recorded in the state).
- Tick-side sweep: a PR with unresolved machine threads and NO agent:rework label and NO rework in flight for >N ticks (e.g. 6) → re-arm agent:rework + comment 'rework arm restored — previous consumption left threads unresolved' (the same recovery the gh-759 sweep does for validation arms).
- Audit log: every consumption records its path (close-bookkeeping / sweep) in the issue comment stream (one short line).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #826 timeline — the bogus consumption is detected ≤6 ticks after it happens and the arm is restored with a comment.
2. AC2: a normal successful rework close still removes the label exactly once, with its marker.
3. AC3: human-thread-only PRs are untouched (gh-744 preserved).
4. AC4: live — after ship, no PR sits >1h in the consumed-without-work state (sweep metric on the board).

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the consumption guard + sweep re-arm.
- L2: replay #826's actual timeline from state snapshots.
- L3 (live): next occurrence self-heals ≤6 ticks.

## Non-goals

- Changing the review/rework verdict semantics.
- gh-744 (never auto-resolve human threads) — untouched.

## References

- Instance: PR #826, evidence comment https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/issues/825#issuecomment-6097560809
- Family: gh-742 (fail-closed), gh-822 (rework bookkeeping), #832 (red-verdict convergence — same pattern class).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 841
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/841
- **Title**: gh-840 [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-840` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +879
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T13:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T13:53:19Z

## PR Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause
- Live PR #826 (gh-825): `agent:rework` was consumed by the `rework-on-label` rule's `consumeLabels` path (dispatch accepted, or gh-715 cross-anchor suppression while a review leg held the other anchor) — yet no rework leg ever ran, no push, 4/6 threads open, no close marker.
- Consumption is fail-open: nothing records it, and every re-arm path (`arm_rework`) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch, gh-807 verdict gate) — the PR hangs forever.

### Fix
- `js/common/reworkConsumption.js` (new): consumption-audit markers (path + head, machine-author-gated) and the pure `shouldRestoreArm` sweep decision.
- `js/smAgent.js`: both `consumeLabels` branches stamp a gh-840 audit comment on every `agent:rework` consumption; new `restore_rework_arm` localAction re-arms when a consumption is proven bogus (marker evidence, head not advanced, no rework in flight, quiet > `staleMinutes`).
- `sm_github.json`: new `rework-arm-restore` rule (machine PRs, unresolved threads, no label; `staleMinutes: 30` ≈ 6 ticks).

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `js/unit-tests/test_reworkConsumption.js` — 16 tests (marker protocol, AC1 restore, AC2 close proofs, AC3 human-only untouched, grace bound). Registered in `run_all.json`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 9 integration tests replaying the #826 timeline (restore, grace, head-advanced, gh-807 gate preserved, human threads, in-flight leg, audit-on-consume, deployed-rule shape).
- Full suite: **2442 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- gh-807 verdict semantics untouched (non-goal); gh-744 preserved — the sweep counts only machine-authored unresolved threads and requires consumption evidence.
- AC4 (live metric) needs post-ship observation; the sweep self-heals the next occurrence ≤6 ticks by construction.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #841._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# 🚨 BLOCKING: the head is read from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules — the entire gh-840 mechanism is inert in production

Both new code paths derive the head only from the query item:

```javascript
var head = ((ticket.pr && ticket.pr.headSha) || ticket.headSha) || null;   // auditReworkConsumption
var head = reworkLatchHeadOf(ticket);                                       // restoreReworkArm
```

For PR-carrier rules, `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` builds items with **`pr: null`** and only populates `item.pr` when `needsStatus` is true — i.e. when the rule query carries `checks` / `mergeState` / `notMergeState` / `mergeable` / `prChecks` / `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` (see the `needsStatus` block and the gh-807 comment above it). Neither consuming rule qualifies:

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`
- `rework-arm-restore` (this PR): `{"type":"pr","notLabels":["agent:rework"],"threadsResolved":false,"prMachineAuthor":true}` → `item.pr` stays `null` (`threadsResolved` reads threads via a separate provider probe; `prMachineAuthor` reads the free `item.author`)

Live consequences, all silent:

1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. The ticket's "Audit log: every consumption records its path" capability never happens, and the sweep has no evidence to ever act on.
2. **The sweep's head-dependent gates are all dead.** `head === null` → `consultReworkLatch` short-circuits to not-latched (gh-806 latch bypassed), the `hasActiveLegRun` check is skipped entirely (in-flight legs don't block the restore), `headAdvanced` is always `false` (the AC2 "head advanced = close proof" branch never fires), the restore marker records head `'unknown'`, and `armReworkLatch(ticket)` no-ops — so after a restore there is no latch protecting against a stacked dispatch.

The 25 tests pass because every fixture injects `pr: { …, headSha: HEAD }` — a shape the live query layer never produces for these two rules. This is exactly the class of bug the tests were meant to exclude.

**Fix:** probe the head through the existing `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` helper (the same fresh-probe pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses at js/smAgent.js:4065) as a fallback in both `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm`, and log a warning when an `agent:rework` consumption cannot be attributed (fail loud, not `return;`). Add at least one test per path with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`) asserting the probe fallback — that test would have caught this.

Related pre-existing note (not this PR's scope, but it shares the same broken assumption): `arm_rework` (`rework-unresolved-threads`, query has no status keys either) also runs with `item.pr === null`, so its gh-806 latch consult/arm is equally inert on the PR-carrier path — worth a follow-up ticket, since it is one of the three "withheld re-arm" causes named in the gh-840 forensics.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: any head move is treated as a rework close — a silent branch refresh after a bogus consumption defeats the sweep permanently

```javascript
var headAdvanced = !!(newestConsume && newestConsume.head && head &&
    String(newestConsume.head) !== String(head));
...
headAdvancedPastConsumption: headAdvanced,
```

The ticket's AC2 close proof is "comment + head advanced **OR** explicit no-threads-to-own proof". This approximation treats *any* head move as the close marker — but `update_branch` (the silent git-merge refresh, js/smAgent.js `silentUpdateBranch`) pushes a merge commit to the PR head **without resolving review threads and without any rework leg running**. Timeline that breaks the sweep:

1. bogus consumption of `agent:rework` (head `H1`, machine threads unresolved) → consume marker stamped for `H1`;
2. the next refresh tick merges `main` → head advances to `H2`, threads untouched;
3. every subsequent sweep: `unresolvedMachineThreads > 0` but `headAdvanced === true` → `'head-advanced'` → **no restore, forever** — the exact consumed-without-work hang this PR exists to fix, now invisible to the recovery path.

The mitigating re-review loop (stale verdict → re-review → fresh verdict → `arm_rework`) may eventually recover such PRs, but gh-840's own forensics show review legs ran repeatedly on #826 for 4h+ without any re-arm landing — relying on that loop is what made the sweep necessary.

**Suggestion:** only accept `head-advanced` as close proof when corroborated — e.g. require a concluded `ai-teammate.yml` leg run on the current head with `created_at` at/after the consumption timestamp (`headWorkflowRunsSafe` is already fetched two lines above for the in-flight check, so this is cheap), or fall through to restore when unresolved *machine* threads still exist on the advanced head (an advanced head with the same open machine threads is evidence of a refresh, not a close). If the deliberate tradeoff is kept, it should be documented in the rule description in `sm_github.json` so the next incident review doesn't misread `'head-advanced'` skips as healthy closes.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# 💡 SUGGESTION: normalize `pullRequestId` to a string for parity with the sibling readers

```javascript
var raw = github_get_pr_comments({
    workspace: repoInfo.owner, repository: repoInfo.repo,
    pullRequestId: prNumber
});
```

Every other caller of `github_get_pr_comments` / `github_get_pr_review_threads` in this codebase passes `pullRequestId: String(prNumber)` (`readVerdictRecords`, `smProvider.verdictRecords`, `prHeadAndLabels`, …). The bridge most likely tolerates a number, but the PR-carrier `ticket.prNumber` type is not guaranteed across all provider paths, and a coercion difference here would silently return zero markers — which for this sweep is the fail-closed "no evidence" shape and thus hard to notice. `String(prNumber)` for consistency.

---

### Thread 4

# gh-840: [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)

## Description

## Goal

`agent:rework` consumption must be FAIL-CLOSED: the label may be removed ONLY by the rework leg's successful close (threads resolved/pushed + 'rework cycle closed' bookkeeping). A consumption without a rework run, a push, or the closing comment is a bug — today it silently hangs the PR forever.

## Subject

The rework-arm consumption path(s) in the SM tick / rework bookkeeping (gh-822 family). Live instance: dmtools-agents PR #826 (gh-825), 2026-10-10 ~10:00Z: `agent:rework` armed (twice, comments present) and later CONSUMED — yet: no fix commit on the head for the review's blocking defect (normTokenRow drops `cacheRead`), 4/6 review threads still unresolved, no 'rework cycle closed' comment, no rework-leg run on the branch (only review legs since 08:55Z). Result: 4h+ hang — gh-744 correctly refuses auto-resolution, nothing re-arms (correct), but the consumed-without-work arm never returns.

## Capability surface

- Guard: label removal only from the leg-close path (verify a closing marker exists: comment + head advanced OR explicit no-threads-to-own proof recorded in the state).
- Tick-side sweep: a PR with unresolved machine threads and NO agent:rework label and NO rework in flight for >N ticks (e.g. 6) → re-arm agent:rework + comment 'rework arm restored — previous consumption left threads unresolved' (the same recovery the gh-759 sweep does for validation arms).
- Audit log: every consumption records its path (close-bookkeeping / sweep) in the issue comment stream (one short line).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #826 timeline — the bogus consumption is detected ≤6 ticks after it happens and the arm is restored with a comment.
2. AC2: a normal successful rework close still removes the label exactly once, with its marker.
3. AC3: human-thread-only PRs are untouched (gh-744 preserved).
4. AC4: live — after ship, no PR sits >1h in the consumed-without-work state (sweep metric on the board).

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the consumption guard + sweep re-arm.
- L2: replay #826's actual timeline from state snapshots.
- L3 (live): next occurrence self-heals ≤6 ticks.

## Non-goals

- Changing the review/rework verdict semantics.
- gh-744 (never auto-resolve human threads) — untouched.

- Instance: PR #826, evidence comment https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/issues/825#issuecomment-6097560809

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

   // silentUpdateBranch's refresh merges also advance the head without a
   // leg. head-advanced only counts when a leg run concluded on the
   // current head at/after the consumption (a real rework close pushes
   // AND resolves via the leg); otherwise the advanced head with the
   // same open machine threads is a refresh, and the sweep proceeds.
   var headAdvanced = !!(newestConsume && newestConsume.head && head &&
       String(newestConsume.head) !== String(head) &&
       hasConcludedLegRunAtOrAfter(headRuns, newestConsume.atMs));

   Wait — but there's a subtlety: `headRuns` is null when probe failed. Then headAdvanced = false → sweep proceeds to restore. Fail-closed toward restore? The current fail-closed philosophy: "a missed sweep retries next tick, a bogus restore arms a duplicate rework leg". Hmm, a bogus restore is worse. But the review explicitly suggests this direction: "fall through to restore when unresolved machine threads still exist on the advanced head (an advanced head with the same open machine threads is evidence of a refresh, not a close)". So proceeding to restore on uncorroborated head advance is the requested behavior.

   Now, what timestamps? A concluded leg run: `status === 'completed'`, path ends with `/ai-teammate.yml`, and `created_at` at/after the consumption timestamp. But wait — should we also require that the run is on the *rework* leg? We can't easily tell leg from workflow runs (the workflow is the same ai-teammate.yml for review and rework legs; inputs differ). The review says "a concluded ai-teammate.yml leg run on the current head with created_at at/after the consumption timestamp". Note that headWorkflowRuns already filters by head_sha, so runs are on the current head. Hmm wait — does headWorkflowRuns filter by head? Let me check line ~4590. Yes: `gh api actions/runs?head_sha=...`. So runs returned are for the current head.

If a review leg concluded on the advanced head after the consumption, we'd count it as corroboration. But per the timeline: bogus consumption at H1, refresh to H2, then... review legs were running on #826 during the hang. Would a review leg run be on head H2? Review legs dispatched before the refresh would be on H1. After the refresh... the re-review loop dispatches review legs on the new head. So a review leg concluding on H2 after consumption could corroborate a false "close". Hmm, but the reviewer's suggested fix is exactly this, so let's not over-engineer. Actually wait — can we distinguish? The workflow run name might include the leg? Not reliably. The suggestion says "e.g." — it's a suggestion. The simpler, more robust alternative within the suggestion: "or fall through to restore when unresolved machine threads still exist on the advanced head". 

   Actually, let me reconsider: maybe combine both criteria from the suggestion:
   - head-advanced accepted as close proof only if corroborated by a concluded leg run on the current head created at/after the consumption timestamp.

   This is what's suggested as primary. I'll implement that. Note `newestConsume.atMs` could be NaN; guard: if…
Now let me look at the rework close bookkeeping and how the rework leg signals a close, plus the test harness mock plumbing.

## PR Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause
- Live PR #826 (gh-825): `agent:rework` was consumed by the `rework-on-label` rule's `consumeLabels` path (dispatch accepted, or gh-715 cross-anchor suppression while a review leg held the other anchor) — yet no rework leg ever ran, no push, 4/6 threads open, no close marker.
- Consumption is fail-open: nothing records it, and every re-arm path (`arm_rework`) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch, gh-807 verdict gate) — the PR hangs forever.

### Fix
- `js/common/reworkConsumption.js` (new): consumption-audit markers (path + head, machine-author-gated) and the pure `shouldRestoreArm` sweep decision.
- `js/smAgent.js`: both `consumeLabels` branches stamp a gh-840 audit comment on every `agent:rework` consumption; new `restore_rework_arm` localAction re-arms when a consumption is proven bogus (marker evidence, head not advanced, no rework in flight, quiet > `staleMinutes`).
- `sm_github.json`: new `rework-arm-restore` rule (machine PRs, unresolved threads, no label; `staleMinutes: 30` ≈ 6 ticks).

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `js/unit-tests/test_reworkConsumption.js` — 16 tests (marker protocol, AC1 restore, AC2 close proofs, AC3 human-only untouched, grace bound). Registered in `run_all.json`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 9 integration tests replaying the #826 timeline (restore, grace, head-advanced, gh-807 gate preserved, human threads, in-flight leg, audit-on-consume, deployed-rule shape).
- Full suite: **2442 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- gh-807 verdict semantics untouched (non-goal); gh-744 preserved — the sweep counts only machine-authored unresolved threads and requires consumption evidence.
- AC4 (live metric) needs post-ship observation; the sweep self-heals the next occurrence ≤6 ticks by construction.

# gh-840: [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)

## Description

## Goal

`agent:rework` consumption must be FAIL-CLOSED: the label may be removed ONLY by the rework leg's successful close (threads resolved/pushed + 'rework cycle closed' bookkeeping). A consumption without a rework run, a push, or the closing comment is a bug — today it silently hangs the PR forever.

## Subject

The rework-arm consumption path(s) in the SM tick / rework bookkeeping (gh-822 family). Live instance: dmtools-agents PR #826 (gh-825), 2026-10-10 ~10:00Z: `agent:rework` armed (twice, comments present) and later CONSUMED — yet: no fix commit on the head for the review's blocking defect (normTokenRow drops `cacheRead`), 4/6 review threads still unresolved, no 'rework cycle closed' comment, no rework-leg run on the branch (only review legs since 08:55Z). Result: 4h+ hang — gh-744 correctly refuses auto-resolution, nothing re-arms (correct), but the consumed-without-work arm never returns.

## Capability surface

- Guard: label removal only from the leg-close path (verify a closing marker exists: comment + head advanced OR explicit no-threads-to-own proof recorded in the state).
- Tick-side sweep: a PR with unresolved machine threads and NO agent:rework label and NO rework in flight for >N ticks (e.g. 6) → re-arm agent:rework + comment 'rework arm restored — previous consumption left threads unresolved' (the same recovery the gh-759 sweep does for validation arms).
- Audit log: every consumption records its path (close-bookkeeping / sweep) in the issue comment stream (one short line).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #826 timeline — the bogus consumption is detected ≤6 ticks after it happens and the arm is restored with a comment.
2. AC2: a normal successful rework close still removes the label exactly once, with its marker.
3. AC3: human-thread-only PRs are untouched (gh-744 preserved).
4. AC4: live — after ship, no PR sits >1h in the consumed-without-work state (sweep metric on the board).

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the consumption guard + sweep re-arm.
- L2: replay #826's actual timeline from state snapshots.
- L3 (live): next occurrence self-heals ≤6 ticks.

## Non-goals

- Changing the review/rework verdict semantics.
- gh-744 (never auto-resolve human threads) — untouched.

## References

- Instance: PR #826, evidence comment https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/issues/825#issuecomment-6097560809
- Family: gh-742 (fail-closed), gh-822 (rework bookkeeping), #832 (red-verdict convergence — same pattern class).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.

## PR Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause
- Live PR #826 (gh-825): `agent:rework` was consumed by the `rework-on-label` rule's `consumeLabels` path (dispatch accepted, or gh-715 cross-anchor suppression while a review leg held the other anchor) — yet no rework leg ever ran, no push, 4/6 threads open, no close marker.
- Consumption is fail-open: nothing records it, and every re-arm path (`arm_rework`) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch, gh-807 verdict gate) — the PR hangs forever.

### Fix
- `js/common/reworkConsumption.js` (new): consumption-audit markers (path + head, machine-author-gated) and the pure `shouldRestoreArm` sweep decision.
- `js/smAgent.js`: both `consumeLabels` branches stamp a gh-840 audit comment on every `agent:rework` consumption; new `restore_rework_arm` localAction re-arms when a consumption is proven bogus (marker evidence, head not advanced, no rework in flight, quiet > `staleMinutes`).
- `sm_github.json`: new `rework-arm-restore` rule (machine PRs, unresolved threads, no label; `staleMinutes: 30` ≈ 6 ticks).

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `js/unit-tests/test_reworkConsumption.js` — 16 tests (marker protocol, AC1 restore, AC2 close proofs, AC3 human-only untouched, grace bound). Registered in `run_all.json`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 9 integration tests replaying the #826 timeline (restore, grace, head-advanced, gh-807 gate preserved, human threads, in-flight leg, audit-on-consume, deployed-rule shape).
- Full suite: **2442 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- gh-807 verdict semantics untouched (non-goal); gh-744 preserved — the sweep counts only machine-authored unresolved threads and requires consumption evidence.
- AC4 (live metric) needs post-ship observation; the sweep self-heals the next occurrence ≤6 ticks by construction.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #841._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# 🚨 BLOCKING: the head is read from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules — the entire gh-840 mechanism is inert in production

Both new code paths derive the head only from the query item:

```javascript
var head = ((ticket.pr && ticket.pr.headSha) || ticket.headSha) || null;   // auditReworkConsumption
var head = reworkLatchHeadOf(ticket);                                       // restoreReworkArm
```

For PR-carrier rules, `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` builds items with **`pr: null`** and only populates `item.pr` when `needsStatus` is true — i.e. when the rule query carries `checks` / `mergeState` / `notMergeState` / `mergeable` / `prChecks` / `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` (see the `needsStatus` block and the gh-807 comment above it). Neither consuming rule qualifies:

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`
- `rework-arm-restore` (this PR): `{"type":"pr","notLabels":["agent:rework"],"threadsResolved":false,"prMachineAuthor":true}` → `item.pr` stays `null` (`threadsResolved` reads threads via a separate provider probe; `prMachineAuthor` reads the free `item.author`)

Live consequences, all silent:

1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. The ticket's "Audit log: every consumption records its path" capability never happens, and the sweep has no evidence to ever act on.
2. **The sweep's head-dependent gates are all dead.** `head === null` → `consultReworkLatch` short-circuits to not-latched (gh-806 latch bypassed), the `hasActiveLegRun` check is skipped entirely (in-flight legs don't block the restore), `headAdvanced` is always `false` (the AC2 "head advanced = close proof" branch never fires), the restore marker records head `'unknown'`, and `armReworkLatch(ticket)` no-ops — so after a restore there is no latch protecting against a stacked dispatch.

The 25 tests pass because every fixture injects `pr: { …, headSha: HEAD }` — a shape the live query layer never produces for these two rules. This is exactly the class of bug the tests were meant to exclude.

**Fix:** probe the head through the existing `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` helper (the same fresh-probe pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses at js/smAgent.js:4065) as a fallback in both `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm`, and log a warning when an `agent:rework` consumption cannot be attributed (fail loud, not `return;`). Add at least one test per path with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`) asserting the probe fallback — that test would have caught this.

Related pre-existing note (not this PR's scope, but it shares the same broken assumption): `arm_rework` (`rework-unresolved-threads`, query has no status keys either) also runs with `item.pr === null`, so its gh-806 latch consult/arm is equally inert on the PR-carrier path — worth a follow-up ticket, since it is one of the three "withheld re-arm" causes named in the gh-840 forensics.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: any head move is treated as a rework close — a silent branch refresh after a bogus consumption defeats the sweep permanently

```javascript
var headAdvanced = !!(newestConsume && newestConsume.head && head &&
    String(newestConsume.head) !== String(head));
...

## Description

## Goal

`agent:rework` consumption must be FAIL-CLOSED: the label may be removed ONLY by the rework leg's successful close (threads resolved/pushed + 'rework cycle closed' bookkeeping). A consumption without a rework run, a push, or the closing comment is a bug — today it silently hangs the PR forever.

## Subject

The rework-arm consumption path(s) in the SM tick / rework bookkeeping (gh-822 family). Live instance: dmtools-agents PR #826 (gh-825), 2026-10-10 ~10:00Z: `agent:rework` armed (twice, comments present) and later CONSUMED — yet: no fix commit on the head for the review's blocking defect (normTokenRow drops `cacheRead`), 4/6 review threads still unresolved, no 'rework cycle closed' comment, no rework-leg run on the branch (only review legs since 08:55Z). - Guard: label removal only from the leg-close path (verify a closing marker exists: comment + head advanced OR explicit no-threads-to-own proof recorded in the state).

1. AC1: replay the #826 timeline — the bogus consumption is detected ≤6 ticks after it happens and the arm is restored with a comment.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

- **PR #**: 841
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/841
- **Title**: gh-840 [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-840` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +879
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T13:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T13:53:19Z

## PR Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause
- Live PR #826 (gh-825): `agent:rework` was consumed by the `rework-on-label` rule's `consumeLabels` path (dispatch accepted, or gh-715 cross-anchor suppression while a review leg held the other anchor) — yet no rework leg ever ran, no push, 4/6 threads open, no close marker.
- Consumption is fail-open: nothing records it, and every re-arm path (`arm_rework`) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch, gh-807 verdict gate) — the PR hangs forever.

### Fix
- `js/common/reworkConsumption.js` (new): consumption-audit markers (path + head, machine-author-gated) and the pure `shouldRestoreArm` sweep decision.
- `js/smAgent.js`: both `consumeLabels` branches stamp a gh-840 audit comment on every `agent:rework` consumption; new `restore_rework_arm` localAction re-arms when a consumption is proven bogus (marker evidence, head not advanced, no rework in flight, quiet > `staleMinutes`).
- `sm_github.json`: new `rework-arm-restore` rule (machine PRs, unresolved threads, no label; `staleMinutes: 30` ≈ 6 ticks).

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `js/unit-tests/test_reworkConsumption.js` — 16 tests (marker protocol, AC1 restore, AC2 close proofs, AC3 human-only untouched, grace bound). Registered in `run_all.json`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 9 integration tests replaying the #826 timeline (restore, grace, head-advanced, gh-807 gate preserved, human threads, in-flight leg, audit-on-consume, deployed-rule shape).
- Full suite: **2442 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- gh-807 verdict semantics untouched (non-goal); gh-744 preserved — the sweep counts only machine-authored unresolved threads and requires consumption evidence.
- AC4 (live metric) needs post-ship observation; the sweep self-heals the next occurrence ≤6 ticks by construction.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #841._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# 🚨 BLOCKING: the head is read from `ticket.pr.headSha`, which is `null` for PR-carrier rules — the entire gh-840 mechanism is inert in production

Both new code paths derive the head only from the query item:

```javascript
var head = ((ticket.pr && ticket.pr.headSha) || ticket.headSha) || null;   // auditReworkConsumption
var head = reworkLatchHeadOf(ticket);                                       // restoreReworkArm
```

For PR-carrier rules, `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` `queryPrs()` builds items with **`pr: null`** and only populates `item.pr` when `needsStatus` is true — i.e. when the rule query carries `checks` / `mergeState` / `notMergeState` / `mergeable` / `prChecks` / `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` (see the `needsStatus` block and the gh-807 comment above it). Neither consuming rule qualifies:

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`
- `rework-arm-restore` (this PR): `{"type":"pr","notLabels":["agent:rework"],"threadsResolved":false,"prMachineAuthor":true}` → `item.pr` stays `null` (`threadsResolved` reads threads via a separate provider probe; `prMachineAuthor` reads the free `item.author`)

Live consequences, all silent:

1. **No audit marker is ever posted.** With `head === null`, `buildConsumeAuditComment()` returns `null` and `auditReworkConsumption` hits `if (!body) return;` — no marker, no warning. The ticket's "Audit log: every consumption records its path" capability never happens, and the sweep has no evidence to ever act on.
2. **The sweep's head-dependent gates are all dead.** `head === null` → `consultReworkLatch` short-circuits to not-latched (gh-806 latch bypassed), the `hasActiveLegRun` check is skipped entirely (in-flight legs don't block the restore), `headAdvanced` is always `false` (the AC2 "head advanced = close proof" branch never fires), the restore marker records head `'unknown'`, and `armReworkLatch(ticket)` no-ops — so after a restore there is no latch protecting against a stacked dispatch.

The 25 tests pass because every fixture injects `pr: { …, headSha: HEAD }` — a shape the live query layer never produces for these two rules. This is exactly the class of bug the tests were meant to exclude.

**Fix:** probe the head through the existing `prHeadAndLabels(repoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` helper (the same fresh-probe pattern `reworkArmGate` already uses at js/smAgent.js:4065) as a fallback in both `auditReworkConsumption` and `restoreReworkArm`, and log a warning when an `agent:rework` consumption cannot be attributed (fail loud, not `return;`). Add at least one test per path with the **live item shape** (`pr: null`) asserting the probe fallback — that test would have caught this.

Related pre-existing note (not this PR's scope, but it shares the same broken assumption): `arm_rework` (`rework-unresolved-threads`, query has no status keys either) also runs with `item.pr === null`, so its gh-806 latch consult/arm is equally inert on the PR-carrier path — worth a follow-up ticket, since it is one of the three "withheld re-arm" causes named in the gh-840 forensics.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# ⚠️ IMPORTANT: any head move is treated as a rework close — a silent branch refresh after a bogus consumption defeats the sweep permanently

```javascript
var headAdvanced = !!(newestConsume && newestConsume.head && head &&
    String(newestConsume.head) !== String(head));
...
headAdvancedPastConsumption: headAdvanced,
```

The ticket's AC2 close proof is "comment + head advanced **OR** explicit no-threads-to-own proof". This approximation treats *any* head move as the close marker — but `update_branch` (the silent git-merge refresh, js/smAgent.js `silentUpdateBranch`) pushes a merge commit to the PR head **without resolving review threads and without any rework leg running**. Timeline that breaks the sweep:

1. bogus consumption of `agent:rework` (head `H1`, machine threads unresolved) → consume marker stamped for `H1`;
2. the next refresh tick merges `main` → head advances to `H2`, threads untouched;
3. every subsequent sweep: `unresolvedMachineThreads > 0` but `headAdvanced === true` → `'head-advanced'` → **no restore, forever** — the exact consumed-without-work hang this PR exists to fix, now invisible to the recovery path.

The mitigating re-review loop (stale verdict → re-review → fresh verdict → `arm_rework`) may eventually recover such PRs, but gh-840's own forensics show review legs ran repeatedly on #826 for 4h+ without any re-arm landing — relying on that loop is what made the sweep necessary.

**Suggestion:** only accept `head-advanced` as close proof when corroborated — e.g. require a concluded `ai-teammate.yml` leg run on the current head with `created_at` at/after the consumption timestamp (`headWorkflowRunsSafe` is already fetched two lines above for the in-flight check, so this is cheap), or fall through to restore when unresolved *machine* threads still exist on the advanced head (an advanced head with the same open machine threads is evidence of a refresh, not a close). If the deliberate tradeoff is kept, it should be documented in the rule description in `sm_github.json` so the next incident review doesn't misread `'head-advanced'` skips as healthy closes.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
# 💡 SUGGESTION: normalize `pullRequestId` to a string for parity with the sibling readers

```javascript
var raw = github_get_pr_comments({
    workspace: repoInfo.owner, repository: repoInfo.repo,
    pullRequestId: prNumber
});
```

Every other caller of `github_get_pr_comments` / `github_get_pr_review_threads` in this codebase passes `pullRequestId: String(prNumber)` (`readVerdictRecords`, `smProvider.verdictRecords`, `prHeadAndLabels`, …). The bridge most likely tolerates a number, but the PR-carrier `ticket.prNumber` type is not guaranteed across all provider paths, and a coercion difference here would silently return zero markers — which for this sweep is the fail-closed "no evidence" shape and thus hard to notice. `String(prNumber)` for consistency.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

# gh-840: [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)

## Description

## Goal

`agent:rework` consumption must be FAIL-CLOSED: the label may be removed ONLY by the rework leg's successful close (threads resolved/pushed + 'rework cycle closed' bookkeeping). A consumption without a rework run, a push, or the closing comment is a bug — today it silently hangs the PR forever.

## Subject

The rework-arm consumption path(s) in the SM tick / rework bookkeeping (gh-822 family). Live instance: dmtools-agents PR #826 (gh-825), 2026-10-10 ~10:00Z: `agent:rework` armed (twice, comments present) and later CONSUMED — yet: no fix commit on the head for the review's blocking defect (normTokenRow drops `cacheRead`), 4/6 review threads still unresolved, no 'rework cycle closed' comment, no rework-leg run on the branch (only review legs since 08:55Z). Result: 4h+ hang — gh-744 correctly refuses auto-resolution, nothing re-arms (correct), but the consumed-without-work arm never returns.

## Capability surface

- Guard: label removal only from the leg-close path (verify a closing marker exists: comment + head advanced OR explicit no-threads-to-own proof recorded in the state).
- Tick-side sweep: a PR with unresolved machine threads and NO agent:rework label and NO rework in flight for >N ticks (e.g. 6) → re-arm agent:rework + comment 'rework arm restored — previous consumption left threads unresolved' (the same recovery the gh-759 sweep does for validation arms).
- Audit log: every consumption records its path (close-bookkeeping / sweep) in the issue comment stream (one short line).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #826 timeline — the bogus consumption is detected ≤6 ticks after it happens and the arm is restored with a comment.
2. AC2: a normal successful rework close still removes the label exactly once, with its marker.
3. AC3: human-thread-only PRs are untouched (gh-744 preserved).
4. AC4: live — after ship, no PR sits >1h in the consumed-without-work state (sweep metric on the board).

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the consumption guard + sweep re-arm.
- L2: replay #826's actual timeline from state snapshots.
- L3 (live): next occurrence self-heals ≤6 ticks.

## Non-goals

- Changing the review/rework verdict semantics.
- gh-744 (never auto-resolve human threads) — untouched.

## References

- Instance: PR #826, evidence comment https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/issues/825#issuecomment-6097560809
- Family: gh-742 (fail-closed), gh-822 (rework bookkeeping), #832 (red-verdict convergence — same pattern class).

- [x] ▶ review (fa-review) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/38056378878) · started 13:37 · done 13:50 ✅

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

So yes, review legs land on the current head.

However — hmm, one more angle: the re-review loop. When does it fire? "stale verdict → re-review". The verdict goes stale after... the head changes! `armReworkDecision`/stale-verdict logic keys on head. A silent refresh advances head → verdict for the OLD head is stale → re-review armed → review leg dispatched on NEW head → concludes → posts verdict marker for new head. So on #826, during a 4h hang with refreshes every tick(?), review legs would conclude on each new head repeatedly. So concluded-leg-run corroboration = false positive in the exact live pathology. CONFIRMED: pure leg-run corroboration is wrong.

So the operative rule must be: **an advanced head with the same unresolved machine threads is a refresh, not a close — fall through to restore.** Combined with keeping a narrow corroborated escape hatch? Any escape hatch needs a signal that a refresh can't produce. Candidates:

Already handled ('no-unresolved-threads'), but note gate order: census check happens in smAgent before calling shouldRestoreArm? No — smAgent passes unresolvedMachineThreads into shouldRestoreArm; pure function checks `> 0` → 'no-unresolved-threads'. ✓
2. A machine-authored marker indicating the threads were addressed on the advanced head — doesn't exist in comment stream.

- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/841
- **Title**: gh-840 [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-840` → `main`

- **Additions**: +879
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T13:36:15Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T13:53:19Z

## PR Description

Closes #840
### Root Cause
- Live PR #826 (gh-825): `agent:rework` was consumed by the `rework-on-label` rule's `consumeLabels` path (dispatch accepted, or gh-715 cross-anchor suppression while a review leg held the other anchor) — yet no rework leg ever ran, no push, 4/6 threads open, no close marker.
- Consumption is fail-open: nothing records it, and every re-arm path (`arm_rework`) is withheld in this state (gh-806 latch, gh-807 verdict gate) — the PR hangs forever.

### Fix
- `js/common/reworkConsumption.js` (new): consumption-audit markers (path + head, machine-author-gated) and the pure `shouldRestoreArm` sweep decision.
- `js/smAgent.js`: both `consumeLabels` branches stamp a gh-840 audit comment on every `agent:rework` consumption; new `restore_rework_arm` localAction re-arms when a consumption is proven bogus (marker evidence, head not advanced, no rework in flight, quiet > `staleMinutes`).
- `sm_github.json`: new `rework-arm-restore` rule (machine PRs, unresolved threads, no label; `staleMinutes: 30` ≈ 6 ticks).

### Test Coverage
- RED→GREEN: `js/unit-tests/test_reworkConsumption.js` — 16 tests (marker protocol, AC1 restore, AC2 close proofs, AC3 human-only untouched, grace bound). Registered in `run_all.json`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 9 integration tests replaying the #826 timeline (restore, grace, head-advanced, gh-807 gate preserved, human threads, in-flight leg, audit-on-consume, deployed-rule shape).
- Full suite: **2442 passed, 0 failed** (`dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

### Notes
- gh-807 verdict semantics untouched (non-goal); gh-744 preserved — the sweep counts only machine-authored unresolved threads and requires consumption evidence.
- AC4 (live metric) needs post-ship observation; the sweep self-heals the next occurrence ≤6 ticks by construction.
