# gh-840: [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)

## Description

## Goal

`agent:rework` consumption must be FAIL-CLOSED: the label may be removed ONLY by the rework leg's successful close (threads resolved/pushed + 'rework cycle closed' bookkeeping). A consumption without a rework run, a push, or the closing comment is a bug — today it silently hangs the PR forever.

## Subject

The rework-arm consumption path(s) in the SM tick / rework bookkeeping (gh-822 family). Live instance: dmtools-agents PR #826 (gh-825), 2026-10-10 ~10:00Z: `agent:rework` armed (twice, comments present) and later CONSUMED — yet: no fix commit on the head for the review's blocking defect (normTokenRow drops `cacheRead`), 4/6 review threads still unresolved, no 'rework cycle closed' comment, no rework-leg run on the branch (only review legs since 08:55Z). Result: 4h+ hang — gh-744 correctly refuses auto-resolution, nothing re-arms (correct), but the consumed-without-work arm never returns.

## Capability surface

- Guard: label removal only from the leg-close path (verify a closing marker exists: comment + head advanced OR explicit no-threads-to-own proof recorded in the state).
- Tick-side sweep: a PR with unresolved machine threads and NO agent:rework label and NO rework in flight for >N ticks (e.g. 6) → re-arm agent:rework + comment 'rework arm restored — previous consumption left threads unresolved' (the same recovery the gh-759 sweep does for validation arms).
- Audit log: every consumption records its path (close-bookkeeping / sweep) in the issue comment stream (one short line).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #826 timeline — the bogus consumption is detected ≤6 ticks after it happens and the arm is restored with a comment.
2. AC2: a normal successful rework close still removes the label exactly once, with its marker.
3. AC3: human-thread-only PRs are untouched (gh-744 preserved).
4. AC4: live — after ship, no PR sits >1h in the consumed-without-work state (sweep metric on the board).

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the consumption guard + sweep re-arm.
- L2: replay #826's actual timeline from state snapshots.
- L3 (live): next occurrence self-heals ≤6 ticks.

## Non-goals

- Changing the review/rework verdict semantics.
- gh-744 (never auto-resolve human threads) — untouched.

## References

- Instance: PR #826, evidence comment https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/issues/825#issuecomment-6097560809
- Family: gh-742 (fail-closed), gh-822 (rework bookkeeping), #832 (red-verdict convergence — same pattern class).

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/38054529577) · started 13:09 · done 13:36 ✅
- [x] ▶ review (fa-review) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/38056378878) · started 13:37 · done 13:50 ✅

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

Both new code paths derive the head only from the query item:

```

Neither consuming rule qualifies:

- `rework-on-label`: `{"type":"pr","labels":["agent:rework"]}` → `item.pr` stays `null`

```javascript

...

# gh-840: [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)

## Description

## Goal

`agent:rework` consumption must be FAIL-CLOSED: the label may be removed ONLY by the rework leg's successful close (threads resolved/pushed + 'rework cycle closed' bookkeeping). A consumption without a rework run, a push, or the closing comment is a bug — today it silently hangs the PR forever.

## Subject

The rework-arm consumption path(s) in the SM tick / rework bookkeeping (gh-822 family). Live instance: dmtools-agents PR #826 (gh-825), 2026-10-10 ~10:00Z: `agent:rework` armed (twice, comments present) and later CONSUMED — yet: no fix commit on the head for the review's blocking defect (normTokenRow drops `cacheRead`), 4/6 review threads still unresolved, no 'rework cycle closed' comment, no rework-leg run on the branch (only review legs since 08:55Z). Result: 4h+ hang — gh-744 correctly refuses auto-resolution, nothing re-arms (correct), but the consumed-without-work arm never returns.

## Capability surface

- Guard: label removal only from the leg-close path (verify a closing marker exists: comment + head advanced OR explicit no-threads-to-own proof recorded in the state).
- Tick-side sweep: a PR with unresolved machine threads and NO agent:rework label and NO rework in flight for >N ticks (e.g. 6) → re-arm agent:rework + comment 'rework arm restored — previous consumption left threads unresolved' (the same recovery the gh-759 sweep does for validation arms).
- Audit log: every consumption records its path (close-bookkeeping / sweep) in the issue comment stream (one short line).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #826 timeline — the bogus consumption is detected ≤6 ticks after it happens and the arm is restored with a comment.
2. AC2: a normal successful rework close still removes the label exactly once, with its marker.
3. AC3: human-thread-only PRs are untouched (gh-744 preserved).
4. AC4: live — after ship, no PR sits >1h in the consumed-without-work state (sweep metric on the board).

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the consumption guard + sweep re-arm.
- L2: replay #826's actual timeline from state snapshots.
- L3 (live): next occurrence self-heals ≤6 ticks.

## Non-goals

- Changing the review/rework verdict semantics.
- gh-744 (never auto-resolve human threads) — untouched.

## References

- Instance: PR #826, evidence comment https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/issues/825#issuecomment-6097560809
- Family: gh-742 (fail-closed), gh-822 (rework bookkeeping), #832 (red-verdict convergence — same pattern class).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

# gh-840: [GOAL] agent:rework consumed WITHOUT the rework leg running — fail-open consumption hangs PRs (live: #826, 4h+ no fix commit, threads open, no close marker)

## Description

## Goal

`agent:rework` consumption must be FAIL-CLOSED: the label may be removed ONLY by the rework leg's successful close (threads resolved/pushed + 'rework cycle closed' bookkeeping). A consumption without a rework run, a push, or the closing comment is a bug — today it silently hangs the PR forever.

## Subject

The rework-arm consumption path(s) in the SM tick / rework bookkeeping (gh-822 family). Live instance: dmtools-agents PR #826 (gh-825), 2026-10-10 ~10:00Z: `agent:rework` armed (twice, comments present) and later CONSUMED — yet: no fix commit on the head for the review's blocking defect (normTokenRow drops `cacheRead`), 4/6 review threads still unresolved, no 'rework cycle closed' comment, no rework-leg run on the branch (only review legs since 08:55Z). Result: 4h+ hang — gh-744 correctly refuses auto-resolution, nothing re-arms (correct), but the consumed-without-work arm never returns.

## Capability surface

- Guard: label removal only from the leg-close path (verify a closing marker exists: comment + head advanced OR explicit no-threads-to-own proof recorded in the state).
- Tick-side sweep: a PR with unresolved machine threads and NO agent:rework label and NO rework in flight for >N ticks (e.g. 6) → re-arm agent:rework + comment 'rework arm restored — previous consumption left threads unresolved' (the same recovery the gh-759 sweep does for validation arms).
- Audit log: every consumption records its path (close-bookkeeping / sweep) in the issue comment stream (one short line).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: replay the #826 timeline — the bogus consumption is detected ≤6 ticks after it happens and the arm is restored with a comment.
2. AC2: a normal successful rework close still removes the label exactly once, with its marker.
3. AC3: human-thread-only PRs are untouched (gh-744 preserved).
4. AC4: live — after ship, no PR sits >1h in the consumed-without-work state (sweep metric on the board).

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the consumption guard + sweep re-arm.
- L2: replay #826's actual timeline from state snapshots.
- L3 (live): next occurrence self-heals ≤6 ticks.

## Non-goals

- Changing the review/rework verdict semantics.
- gh-744 (never auto-resolve human threads) — untouched.

## References

- Instance: PR #826, evidence comment https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/issues/825#issuecomment-6097560809
- Family: gh-742 (fail-closed), gh-822 (rework bookkeeping), #832 (red-verdict convergence — same pattern class).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

OK. Let me settle the design. The reviewer's primary suggestion has the review-leg false-positive hole I identified. The alternative — "fall through to restore when unresolved machine threads still exist on the advanced head" — is simple, robust, and directly targets the failure: an advanced head with the same open machine threads = refresh, not close.

But then what role does `headAdvancedPastConsumption` play at all? With option (b): if machineThreads > 0 → restore regardless of head. If machineThreads === 0 → 'no-unresolved-threads'. So the head-advanced gate becomes unreachable... UNLESS we still want it for the case where a concluded rework leg on the current head proves close DESPITE open threads. Hmm.

Wait, actually, let me re-read the pure function's contract. The order:

```javascript
if (!(Number(s.unresolvedMachineThreads) > 0)) return 'no-unresolved-threads';
if (s.headAdvancedPastConsumption) return 'head-advanced';
```

What scenario is 'head-advanced' protecting? Consider a PR where the rework leg pushed commits (head advanced) but the machine threads are STILL OPEN — e.g. the leg addressed some threads, pushed, and the remaining threads... no wait, if threads are open and machine-authored, more rework is needed, so restoring the arm is right.

Consider: rework leg ran, pushed fix for blocking issue, resolved threads it fixed, but left some machine threads open intentionally? Doesn't happen in this system — machine threads are the reviewer's and get resolved by the leg when addressed.

Consider the AC2 test in the existing suite: "head advanced past the consumption (a real push/close) → no restore". The fixture has threads OPEN (threadsPayload('ai-teammate', false)) AND head advanced. So the intended semantic in the current implementation: push = close proof even with open threads. But per the reviewer, that's exactly wrong for the refresh case.

So what distinguishes the existing AC2 test scenario from the refresh scenario? In AC2, a rework leg... in the fixture there's no leg run; it's just "head advanced". The reviewer's point: that fixture shape (head advanced, threads open, no leg run) is ALSO the silent-refresh shape. They're observationally identical except for the workflow runs.

Given they're identical without leg-run data, the only distinguishing signal IS the workflow run rollup. And my objection was: review legs (not rework legs) also produce concluded runs on the current head, and those were running during the #826 hang. BUT — wait. Let me re-examine: were review legs concluding on the CURRENT head during the hang? The review legs dispatched during the hang were dispatched on whatever head existed at dispatch time. The hang scenario in the reviewer's thread 2:

1. bogus consumption at H1 → marker stamped H1.
2. refresh tick merges main → H2.
3. sweeps: threads open, headAdvanced (H1≠H2) → suppressed forever.

In this scenario, are there leg runs on H2? Only if something dispatches legs on H2 after the refresh. The re-review loop (stale verdict → re-review) might. On #826, review legs ran repeatedly — before the refresh (heads H0→H1?) and possibly after. If a review leg concluded on H2 at/after the consumption timestamp, corroboration fires → suppression → hang persists. The reviewer's own text acknowledges this loop may not recover: "gh-840's own forensics show review legs ran repeatedly on #826 for 4h+ without any re-arm landing — relying on that loop is what made the sweep necessary."

So a corroboration that any ai-teammate.yml run (including review legs) satisfies is self-defeating on the live instance. Can we require the concluded run to be a REWORK leg? Not distinguishable via the list API. Hmm.

BUT: here's a thought — the verdict record! Review legs post gh-807 verdict markers (machine-parsed). A review leg concluding on the current head produces a verdict marker with `head: H2`. Hmm interesting: so if review legs keep concluding REQUEST_CHANGES on H2, the gate passes, and then... if we suppress via head-advanced-corroborated-by-any-leg-run, the sweep is suppressed forever. If instead we treat "advanced head with open machine threads" as a refresh → restore fires → arm restored → rework-on-label dispatches a rework leg. Correct!

So final design (option b + documented tradeoff):

**The head-advanced gate only suppresses when the head advance is corroborated by close evidence. Given observationally-identical shapes, the deciding rule: unresolved machine threads on the advanced head = work not done = refresh, not close. Therefore: when the machine-thread census is non-zero, an uncorroborated... **

Ugh, I keep going in circles. DECISION TIME.

Design: keep the pure `shouldRestoreArm` shape but change the head-advanced semantics via a new input. Actually — simpler: change smAgent's `headAdvanced` computation to require corroboration by a concluded **rework** leg run, and since we can't distinguish review from rework runs, require corroboration by a concluded leg run on the current head created at/after the consumption **AND**... no.

Hmm hold on, WAIT. Let me check `armReworkDecision` semantics — maybe a REQUEST_CHANGES verdict at/after consumption with blocking census is itself the "evidence a rework leg is needed" and the sweep restoring is correct. Yes — that's the design: the verdict gate only withholds on APPROVE.

OK so truly final: I'll implement the reviewer's alternative as the mechanism, because the primary is observably self-defeating on the live instance:

**In `restoreReworkArm`: compute `headAdvanced` as before, but pass a corroboration flag; the sweep treats an advanced head as close proof ONLY when a concluded leg run exists on the current head created at/after the newest consumption timestamp — and if not corroborated, the sweep falls through to the restore decision (an advanced head with the same open machine threads is a refresh, not a close). A review leg on H2 concluding after the refresh.

UNLESS the corroborating run must be on the CONSUMED head (H1): the closing leg was dispatched on H1 (consumed head) — the consumption happened because rework-on-label dispatched on H1! So: a successful close = the leg dispatched on H1 concluded (rollup(H1) has concluded run at/after consumption) AND head advanced past H1. ## Design decision for Thread 2 (IMPORTANT)

I'll implement the corroboration in `smAgent.js` (impure layer, has workflow-run access) while keeping the pure module's contract: `headAdvancedPastConsumption` becomes a *corroborated* close proof computed by the caller. Concretely:

The reviewer's suggested corroboration: "require a concluded `ai-teammate.yml` leg run on the current head with `created_at` at/after the consumption timestamp". My analysis showed review-leg false positives. But wait — let me re-examine once more. Does a review leg actually land ON the PR head? Let me check how review legs are dispatched — `workflowRef: '{branch}'`. A run dispatched on branch records the branch's head AT DISPATCH TIME as head_sha. So yes, review legs land on the current head.

However — hmm, one more angle: the re-review loop. When does it fire? "stale verdict → re-review". The verdict goes stale after... the head changes! `armReworkDecision`/stale-verdict logic keys on head. A silent refresh advances head → verdict for the OLD head is stale → re-review armed → review leg dispatched on NEW head → concludes → posts verdict marker for new head. So on #826, during a 4h hang with refreshes every tick(?), review legs would conclude on each new head repeatedly. So concluded-leg-run corroboration = false positive in the exact live pathology. CONFIRMED: pure leg-run corroboration is wrong.

So the operative rule must be: **an advanced head with the same unresolved machine threads is a refresh, not a close — fall through to restore.** Combined with keeping a narrow corroborated escape hatch? Any escape hatch needs a signal that a refresh can't produce. Candidates:
1. Machine-thread census clean (threads resolved) — primary close proof. Already handled ('no-unresolved-threads'), but note gate order: census check happens in smAgent before calling shouldRestoreArm? No — smAgent passes unresolvedMachineThreads into shouldRestoreArm; pure function checks `> 0` → 'no-unresolved-threads'. ✓
2. A machine-authored marker indicating the threads were addressed on the advanced head — doesn't exist in comment stream.

So: no reliable escape hatch beyond the census. The head-advanced suppression must go (when machine threads are open). 

Now, how to structure the change to keep the pure module meaningful? Option: change the pure function to REMOVE the headAdvancedPastConsumption input and the 'head-advanced' reason. Update doc. The smAgent stops computing headAdvanced for the decision (still computes head for latch/in-flight/marker).

Wait, but hmm, let me reconsider gate ordering effects: currently `headAdvancedPastConsumption` check sits between census and evidence checks. Removing it: head advanced + threads open + evidence + stale → restore. AC2 close (threads resolved) → census 0 → 'no-unresolved-threads'. ✓ AC2 "removes the label exactly once, with its marker" — the close path (pushReworkChanges) removes labels itself; sweep doesn't touch. ✓

Risk: partial rework — leg pushed, resolved SOME machine threads, others still open, leg concluded, label already consumed at dispatch. Sweep: threads open (machine), evidence (consume marker), stale → restore → re-dispatch rework leg. Desired? The rework isn't done (threads open) → yes, restore is the fail-closed behavior. The restore marker keeps the cycle bounded (gh-821-style durability, within-grace bound). ✓ And the gh-806 latch set by armReworkLatch after restore prevents stacking.

But wait — there's a subtlety: after a REAL successful rework close that resolved threads, could the sweep still fire? Census 0 → no. What if the leg resolved threads but the census probe fails (-1) → fail closed, retry next tick ✓.

Now, is removing the head-advanced check entirely the right call vs. keeping it corroborated-only? Consider: restore fires after silent refresh → arm restored → rework-on-label dispatches leg on new head → leg works → fine. Consider pathological: refresh keeps happening every tick (update_branch cron), each refresh advances head → consume marker head H1 ≠ current → with old code: suppressed forever. With new code: restore fires once (quiet window from consumption > stale) → arm restored → latch armed (pr, H2). Next tick: rework-on-label dispatches (label present). Leg runs on H2. Meanwhile the sweep rule: notLabels agent:rework → after restore the label is present → sweep rule doesn't match. ✓ The latch (gh-806) prevents double dispatch from other armers. Good.

Edge: after restore + re-consumption without work (another bogus consume at H2, marker head H2), refresh to H3... sweep: newest consume head H2, current head H3, threads open, quiet since newest consume... restores again. Bounded cycle by design. ✓

OK — final: remove head-advanced suppression from pure module; document tradeoff in sm_github.json rule description; smAgent simplifies (no headAdvanced computation for the decision, but still needs head for latch + in-flight + marker).

Hmm, wait — actually, hold on. Let me reconsider keeping the input but with new semantics one more. The concern with fully removing: the reviewer offered corroboration first. But they explicitly offered the alternative. Since I can justify with the live forensics (review legs running 4h+ on #826 — corroboration by any leg run would self-defeat), removing is right. I'll explain this in the reply.

Actually — one middle ground worth considering: keep the pure-function input but make smAgent pass `headAdvancedPastConsumption: false` always... no, that's dead code. Remove cleanly.

Wait, actually, let me reconsider ONE more scenario for keeping a narrow corroboration: the rework leg that concludes and pushes ALSO resolves threads via API. So after a real close, census = 0. There's NO healthy path where a real close leaves machine threads open. The suppression only ever fired for refresh/partial states, both of which should restore. Removing is strictly more correct. DONE deliberating.

## Changes

### 1. `js/common/reworkConsumption.js`
- Remove `headAdvancedPastConsumption` from `shouldRestoreArm` + doc updates. Keep everything else.

### 2. `js/smAgent.js`
- `auditReworkConsumption`: probe fallback via `prHeadAndLabels` + fail-loud warning when head unattributable.

- `prCommentList`: `pullRequestId: String(prNumber)`.
- `consultReworkLatch(key, ticket, effectiveRepoInfo, headOverride)`.
- `armReworkLatch(ticket, headOverride)`.

### 3. `sm_github.json`

**test_reworkConsumption.js** (TDD: RED first):

  - sweep with pr:null and probe failure → no restore, warning (fail loud, no crash).
- The verdict-gate AC2 test still passes (verdict APPROVE withholds before evidence check). ✓

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. ## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

## Design decision for Thread 2 (IMPORTANT)

I'll implement the corroboration in `smAgent.js` (impure layer, has workflow-run access) while keeping the pure module's contract: `headAdvancedPastConsumption` becomes a *corroborated* close proof computed by the caller. Concretely:

The reviewer's suggested corroboration: "require a concluded `ai-teammate.yml` leg run on the current head with `created_at` at/after the consumption timestamp". My analysis showed review-leg false positives. But wait — let me re-examine once more. Does a review leg actually land ON the PR head? Let me check how review legs are dispatched — `workflowRef: '{branch}'`. A run dispatched on branch records the branch's head AT DISPATCH TIME as head_sha. So yes, review legs land on the current head.

However — hmm, one more angle: the re-review loop. When does it fire? "stale verdict → re-review". The verdict goes stale after... the head changes! `armReworkDecision`/stale-verdict logic keys on head. A silent refresh advances head → verdict for the OLD head is stale → re-review armed → review leg dispatched on NEW head → concludes → posts verdict marker for new head. So on #826, during a 4h hang with refreshes every tick(?), review legs would conclude on each new head repeatedly. So concluded-leg-run corroboration = false positive in the exact live pathology. CONFIRMED: pure leg-run corroboration is wrong.

So the operative rule must be: **an advanced head with the same unresolved machine threads is a refresh, not a close — fall through to restore.** Combined with keeping a narrow corroborated escape hatch? Any escape hatch needs a signal that a refresh can't produce. Candidates:
1. Machine-thread census clean (threads resolved) — primary close proof. Already handled ('no-unresolved-threads'), but note gate order: census check happens in smAgent before calling shouldRestoreArm? No — smAgent passes unresolvedMachineThreads into shouldRestoreArm; pure function checks `> 0` → 'no-unresolved-threads'. ✓
2. A machine-authored marker indicating the threads were addressed on the advanced head — doesn't exist in comment stream.

So: no reliable escape hatch beyond the census. The head-advanced suppression must go (when machine threads are open). 

Now, how to structure the change to keep the pure module meaningful? Option: change the pure function to REMOVE the headAdvancedPastConsumption input and the 'head-advanced' reason. Update doc. The smAgent stops computing headAdvanced for the decision (still computes head for latch/in-flight/marker).

Wait, but hmm, let me reconsider gate ordering effects: currently `headAdvancedPastConsumption` check sits between census and evidence checks. Removing it: head advanced + threads open + evidence + stale → restore. AC2 close (threads resolved) → census 0 → 'no-unresolved-threads'. ✓ AC2 "removes the label exactly once, with its marker" — the close path (pushReworkChanges) removes labels itself; sweep doesn't touch. ✓

Risk: partial rework — leg pushed, resolved SOME machine threads, others still open, leg concluded, label already consumed at dispatch. Sweep: threads open (machine), evidence (consume marker), stale → restore → re-dispatch rework leg. Desired? The rework isn't done (threads open) → yes, restore is the fail-closed behavior. The restore marker keeps the cycle bounded (gh-821-style durability, within-grace bound). ✓ And the gh-806 latch set by armReworkLatch after restore prevents stacking.

But wait — there's a subtlety: after a REAL successful rework close that resolved threads, could the sweep still fire? Census 0 → no. What if the leg resolved threads but the census probe fails (-1) → fail closed, retry next tick ✓.

Now, is removing the head-advanced check entirely the right call vs. keeping it corroborated-only? Consider: restore fires after silent refresh → arm restored → rework-on-label dispatches leg on new head → leg works → fine. Consider pathological: refresh keeps happening every tick (update_branch cron), each refresh advances head → consume marker head H1 ≠ current → with old code: suppressed forever. With new code: restore fires once (quiet window from consumption > stale) → arm restored → latch armed (pr, H2). Next tick: rework-on-label dispatches (label present). Leg runs on H2. Meanwhile the sweep rule: notLabels agent:rework → after restore the label is present → sweep rule doesn't match. ✓ The latch (gh-806) prevents double dispatch from other armers. Good.

Edge: after restore + re-consumption without work (another bogus consume at H2, marker head H2), refresh to H3... sweep: newest consume head H2, current head H3, threads open, quiet since newest consume... restores again. Bounded cycle by design. ✓

OK — final: remove head-advanced suppression from pure module; document tradeoff in sm_github.json rule description; smAgent simplifies (no headAdvanced computation for the decision, but still needs head for latch + in-flight + marker).

Hmm, wait — actually, hold on. Let me reconsider keeping the input but with new semantics one more. The concern with fully removing: the reviewer offered corroboration first. But they explicitly offered the alternative. Since I can justify with the live forensics (review legs running 4h+ on #826 — corroboration by any leg run would self-defeat), removing is right. I'll explain this in the reply.

Actually — one middle ground worth considering: keep the pure-function input but make smAgent pass `headAdvancedPastConsumption: false` always... no, that's dead code. Remove cleanly.

Wait, actually, let me reconsider ONE more scenario for keeping a narrow corroboration: the rework leg that concludes and pushes ALSO resolves threads via API. So after a real close, census = 0. There's NO healthy path where a real close leaves machine threads open. The suppression only ever fired for refresh/partial states, both of which should restore. Removing is strictly more correct. DONE deliberating.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```
